In [23]:
print("Missing Values:", df.isnull().sum().sum())
print("Duplicate Rows:", df.duplicated().sum())
print("Shape:", df.shape)

Missing Values: 0
Duplicate Rows: 897
Shape: (2109, 22)
  • From above output we can see that one duplicate rows occur 50+ or even 100+ times
  • They are not data entry errors; they represent different software modules with identical metric values.
  • Duplicate records were retained because they represent valid software modules
  • with identical software metrics in the original NASA PROMISE KC1 dataset.
  • Removing them could distort the original data distribution.
  • The NASA PROMISE KC1 dataset is commonly used this way in software defect prediction research.

ROC Curve¶

In [46]:
fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_prob_lr)

plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
plt.plot(fpr, tpr, label="Logistic Regression")
plt.plot([0,1],[0,1],'--')

plt.xlabel("False Positive Rate")
plt.ylabel("True Positive Rate")
plt.title("ROC Curve")

plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(os.path.join(output_dir, "lr_roc_curve.png"), dpi=300)
plt.show()

Observation:¶

  • High accuracy but low recall.
  • The model misses many defective modules, so there is room for improvement with Random Forest, XGBoost, and later SMOTE.

Observation¶

  • XGBoost achieved the highest Accuracy, Recall, and F1-score, indicating the best overall defect prediction performance.
  • Random Forest achieved the highest ROC-AUC, suggesting strong discriminative ability.
  • Logistic Regression had the highest Precision, but its low Recall means it missed many defective modules.
